description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 1630-1637: is_aia_recoverable matches against a SHORT explicit list of pkix_path::Error variants (ChainBroken, NoTrustedPath, SignatureInvalid), not against a 'is it a fatal cert-level error' negative list.

WHY THIS IS CORRECT: the allowlist approach means new pkix_path::Error variants are by default NOT considered AIA-recoverable. A future variant like RevocationStatusUnknown or HsmSignatureRequired added to pkix_path will not silently trigger pointless AIA round-trips. The reviewer adding the new variant has to explicitly decide whether AIA fetching can fix that condition; the answer is no for almost every cert-level defect.

The docstring (lines 1614-1629) explicitly lists 'all other variants (ValidityPeriod, KeyUsageMissing, NameConstraintViolation, PolicyViolation, Der, …) describe cert-level defects that the chain-build seam cannot fix by adding more certs, so they are propagated directly without ever invoking the AiaFetcher.' The rationale is captured next to the code.

WHAT A FUTURE CONTRIBUTOR MIGHT WRONGLY SUGGEST: 'invert the match — list the non-recoverable errors and recover by default.' That suggestion produces the silent-pointless-fetch hazard: a new error variant becomes recoverable without explicit review.

Two test cases ground the allowlist's behaviour:
- non_recoverable_path_error_does_not_invoke_aia (tests/aia_chain_build.rs:206) — expired leaf surfaces directly without AIA.
- aia_fetches_missing_intermediate_and_chain_validates (tests/aia_chain_build.rs:85) — ChainBroken triggers AIA and succeeds.

DEFEND IF: someone suggests inverting the match, adding more variants to the recoverable list without test coverage, or removing the comment that documents WHY the list is short.
title: is_aia_recoverable allowlist (not denylist) of pkix_path errors that may benefit from AIA augmentation
